prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1429; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record. Actually, we can skip that for this recording. Can you tell me where and when the accident happened?
A: It happened on a two-lane road in Baytown, Texas, in the late afternoon. I'd been driving home from work.

Q: Walk me through what happened before the impact.
A: I was heading east, going maybe thirty miles an hour because traffic was slow. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane while trying to pass a slower vehicle.

Q: Did you have time to react?
A: Not really. I hit the brakes and turned a little to the right, but we still collided nearly head-on. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The steering wheel and the dashboard were close to my knee, though, and that's where I felt the pain.

Q: Tell me about your injury.
A: My right knee struck the lower part of the dashboard. It swelled up within a couple of hours and I've had trouble bending it and putting weight on it since then.

Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes. A paramedic checked me at the scene, and I went to an urgent care clinic later that evening. They took X-rays and sent me for a follow-up with a specialist.

Q: Have you missed any work?
A: Yes, I've been off for a few days and I'm on light duty now.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?
A: Only that the other driver apologized at the scene and gave me their insurance information. That's about all I can add.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thanks.
